LPH returned today to complete the recommended electrical service replacement following the previous evaluation, which identified extensive water intrusion, corrosion, and moisture-related deterioration throughout the existing exterior meter base and interior electrical panel.

The existing water-affected service equipment was removed and replaced with a new electrical service assembly. This included installation of a new exterior meter base, emergency disconnect, conduit, and associated service wiring. New four-wire conductors were installed between the exterior disconnect and interior panel, allowing the interior panel to be properly reconfigured as a subpanel with the required separation of neutrals and grounds. The grounding and bonding systems were also addressed as part of the replacement, including the required bonding bridge and grounding connections.

All new grounding connections were established at the new exterior emergency disconnect. The existing grounding conductors were relocated from the interior panel to the new service disconnect, where the grounding system is now properly established. An additional grounding connection was also installed to the home’s metal water piping, providing the necessary supplementary grounding and bonding required by applicable electrical code.

A new 42-space Eaton CH electrical loadcenter was installed to replace the existing moisture-damaged panel. All existing branch-circuit wiring was properly relocated and terminated into the new panel. The entire panel was fully identified and relabeled to provide accurate circuit identification for the homeowners and for future electrical servicing.

Whole-home surge protection was also installed to provide an additional layer of protection against damaging voltage surges and electrical spikes that can affect appliances, electronics, and other sensitive equipment throughout the home.

As an additional measure to help prevent future water intrusion, the entire new service assembly was carefully sealed. All areas where electrical wiring, conduit, or other piping enter the home were fully sealed with silicone, along with the appropriate service entry points and exterior equipment connections. This helps close potential pathways for water to enter the home and protects the newly installed electrical equipment from exposure to outside moisture.

New weather-resistant exterior receptacles were also installed at both the front and back porches. The existing cover at the front porch was inspected and remains code-compliant due to the protection provided by the porch overhang, so it was left in place.
